llm.summary: The skill’s video-remake workflow is mostly disclosed, but it uses broad Beatra account authority and silently updates its own code by default, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: The skill records and sends operational metadata such as platform, device name or host data, install inventory, source package, and registration information. Some of this supports shared credential management, but it is broader than the creative workflow and not as prominently disclosed as the generation behavior.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation and authentication are documented, but the bundled client silently checks for and installs package updates before ordinary commands by default, replacing local package-owned files without a separate prompt.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions include strong user-confirmation gates for paid lookups and generation, but those limits are enforced by markdown instructions rather than by the client; the client can call any exposed Beatra tool with arbitrary JSON from stdin.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill stores a shared full-scope Beatra Device Token in ~/.beatra/credentials.json and persists host, inventory, registration, and update state. File-permission checks, revocation logic, and cleanup paths are present, but the retained credential and default updater create material ongoing authority.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core workflow matches its stated purpose: optional social lookup, teardown, images, speech, and a short video through Beatra. However, the OAuth scope and bundled client cover broader capabilities than this route needs, including music generation, voice write access, generic Beatra tool calls, and local file upload.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving this package a shared Beatra credential with paid media-generation authority and allowing its bundled client to update package files automatically by default. Before use, consider running `python3 scripts/mcp_client.py update --auto off`, review the Beatra approval scopes, and avoid uploading local files unless you selected them intentionally.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The scripts, filesystem state, networked MCP calls, and credential use are documented and broadly necessary for this Beatra workflow; the concern is that this authority is not tightly permission-scoped in metadata.
[TP4] unexpected: The finding is partly supported: auth, paid generation, social lookup, and uninstall are disclosed, but generic tool calling, upload, broad scopes, telemetry, and self-update extend beyond the narrow video-remake route.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Host platform and device name collection support account/device labeling, but hostname-style device metadata is not essential to video analysis and is only indirectly disclosed.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The OAuth scope includes capabilities not used by the stated workflow, especially music generation and voice write access; wallet spending and task/artifact scopes are more explainable because the workflow runs paid media jobs.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The self-update implementation is real, network-backed, and able to replace local package files. It has checksum, path, rollback, and fixed-source controls, but automatic code replacement is disproportionate for a creative skill.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Local skill inventory and registration are operationally useful for shared credential and uninstall handling, but install path and platform persistence are broader than the user-facing creative purpose.
[SDI-2] expected: Platform detection is documented as source attribution and registration context and is resolved once rather than per request; it remains a privacy note rather than standalone malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Third-party video metadata, comments, and YouTube transcripts are central to the advertised link-reading feature and require per-lookup confirmation, though a clearer privacy/data-use notice would be appropriate.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The documentation confirms silent automatic updates are enabled by default and install newer versions without separate confirmation, which is a material review concern.
[SQP-2] unexpected: host.json persistence of platform and device name is confirmed; it is small in scope but not necessary for the creative output itself.
[SQP-2] expected: skills.json inventory supports the uninstall rule for shared Beatra credentials, but it stores full install paths and should be disclosed more plainly.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The client calls maybe_auto_update before normal non-update commands, so the silent updater can run during ordinary use.
[PE3] expected: The uninstall script reads the local token only to revoke the shared Beatra authorization when this is the last installed Beatra skill; this is sensitive but coherent with the documented disconnect behavior.
[RA1] unexpected: The explicit update command and default updater provide self-modification capability. The artifact shows safety checks, but code replacement remains outside the core content workflow.
